pergunta: Of which population is E_sigma[Err_sigma] (mean MAE over split draws of the retained test set, which is what the protocol reports) an estimator, and with what bias relative to the MAE of the whole domain? Does the mean weighted by p_i^te (Sum p_i e_i / Sum p_i) reproduce E_sigma[Err_sigma] closely enough to become the formal definition of the estimand in Sec.3? Does the Horvitz-Thompson correction (1 split draw, weighted by 1/p_i^te) reduce the bias enough to enter the article?
alegacao: A3 (estimand drift) + formal estimand of Sec.3 (D6-i)

criterio.pergunta: Of which population is E_sigma[Err_sigma] (mean MAE over split draws of the retained test set, which is what the protocol reports) an estimator, and with what bias relative to the MAE of the whole domain? Does the mean weighted by p_i^te (Sum p_i e_i / Sum p_i) reproduce E_sigma[Err_sigma] closely enough to become the formal definition of the estimand in Sec.3? Does the Horvitz-Thompson correction (1 split draw, weighted by 1/p_i^te) reduce the bias enough to enter the article?
criterio.alegacao: A3 (estimand drift) + formal estimand of Sec.3 (D6-i)
criterio.hipotese: with FIXED e_i (predictors without training, constant and FSPL calibrated on the valid training nodes, calibrated ONCE on the reference split seed=42), Sum p_i e_i/Sum p_i (ratio of expectations, using p_i^te from test 1.6) approximates E_sigma[Err_sigma] (expectation of the ratio) better than the MAE of the whole domain; the single-draw Horvitz-Thompson correction may or may not reduce the bias relative to the whole-domain MAE
criterio.metodo_fixado: same 4 cells and 100 seeds as test 1.6 (identical split, reuse of the same partitions per split draw); e_i = |y_i - yhat_i| in RSSI for EVERY node of the domain (3600x3600), fixed by ONE calibration on the training set of split seed=42 (constant=median(RSSI_train); calibrated FSPL (b) = offset by the median of the VALID training nodes, frozen okumura/fspl formula from scripts_congelados/baselines_v2_por_particao.py); per population (valid: PL<299, sentinel: PL>=299, all): (a) whole-domain MAE = mean(e_i) over all nodes of the population; (b) mean over the 100 split draws of MAE(e_i) restricted to the retained test set V_te(sigma); (c) Sum_{i in population} p_i^te e_i / Sum_{i in population} p_i^te (p_i^te from test 1.6, same 100 draws); (d) per-draw Horvitz-Thompson: Sum_{i in V_te(sigma) intersect population} e_i/p_i^te / Sum_{i in V_te(sigma) intersect population} 1/p_i^te, mean and std over the 100 draws.
criterio.definicoes: vies_protocolo = (b) - (a); vies_HT = mean(d) - (a); (b)-(c) measures the ratio of expectations (c) vs the expectation of the ratio (b). Everything in dB (RSSI), 3 decimal places.
criterio.limiar_aceitacao: (c) reproduces (b) within <0.05 dB in >=3 of the 4 cells (then Sum p_i e_i/Sum p_i becomes the publishable formal definition of the estimand in Sec.3); the HT correction enters the article only if |vies_HT| < |vies_protocolo|/2 in >=3 of the 4 cells AND in the three populations (valid, sentinel, all) simultaneously
criterio.refutacao: if (c) diverges from (b) by >=0.05 dB in >=2 of the 4 cells, the ratio of expectations is not declared equivalent to the expectation of the ratio and Sec.3 must record the difference as a note, not as an identity; if the HT bias-reduction condition fails in any population or in <3 cells, the HT correction LEAVES the article (only the definition + the reported bias remain)

metodo: same 4 cells and 100 split draws as 1.6; fixed e_i calibrated on split seed=42 (constant=median(RSSI_tr); FSPL(b)=offset by the median of the valid training nodes), applied to every node of the domain; (a) MAE over the whole domain; (b) mean over 100 split draws of the MAE on the held-out test set (only in draws with M_sigma>0, event A_U); (c) Sum p_i^te e_i / Sum p_i^te (the whole population domain); (d) Horvitz-Thompson per split draw, mean and SD over 100 split draws; M_sigma/Err_sigma per split draw and w_i by accumulation (see erratum).
nota_seeds_compartilhados: the 4 cells share the same mesh of N=132 blocks and the SAME 100 seeds (they are not independent Monte Carlo replicates).

errata.adicionado: records per split draw the pair (M_sigma, Err_sigma) per population and predictor (field M_sigma_todos_100, 100 values including M=0); reports n_sorteios_M_igual_0 and n_sorteios_A_M_maior_0; computes E[M|A], CV(M|A), Cov(Err_sigma,M|A)/E[M|A] and numerically checks the identity Err(U)-theta_U = -Cov(Err_sigma,M_U|A)/E[M_U|A] (prop:ratio(iii) of internal/note_26.md; field identidade_residuo_lhs_menos_termo, must be ~0 -- confirmed <1e-6 in all cell x population x predictor pairs with n_A>=2). w_i computed by accumulating 1{i in V_te(sigma)}/M_sigma over the draws with M_sigma>0, divided by n_A (estimate of E[1{i in V}/M|A], prop:ratio(ii)); soma_w_i must be ~1 and Err_via_w_i_dB must reproduce (b).
errata.conclusao_HT_mantida: the Horvitz-Thompson correction REMAINS out of the article (pre-registered decision criterion not met: |vies_HT| does not fall below |vies_protocolo|/2 in >=3 cells x 3 populations). BUT the reason stated in fismat_vies_ht.json is stronger than 'the criterion was not met': the 'halves it' criterion itself was set WITHIN the Monte Carlo noise -- the HT estimate varies by 7.8 to 9.1 dB from split draw to split draw (d_HT_dp_dB, valid population, constant predictor), i.e. 13 to 30 times the very bias it should remove, and the indicative vies_HT_em_SE stays at -0.57..0.54 (indistinguishable from zero at 100 draws). The correct reading is not 'the HT failed the criterion' but 'the correction is not resolvable with this number of draws and does not gain in per-draw MSE' -- it leaves the article all the same, but for this stronger reason.
errata.nota_seeds_compartilhados: as in 1.6: the 4 cells use the SAME mesh (N=132) and the SAME 100 seeds; sign agreement between cells in the fields vies_protocolo/vies_HT is NOT independent Monte Carlo replication.

resumo.regra_c_ok: >=3 of the 4 cells in at least one predictor
resumo.regra_HT_ok: >=3 of the 4 cells AND in the 3 populations simultaneously
